_doc: Seconds each step of .github/workflows/pages.yml may take, keyed 'job/step name'. tools/step_budgets.py check-run fails the build job's last step on a step over its budget or with no row; tests/test_step_budgets.sh fails on a step with no row, and on a step that reads the whole corpus without naming the cache it restores ('cache'), how it limits itself to what changed ('incremental'), or why it can do neither ('uncached'). Raise a budget only with the reason in the commit: a budget that moves with every slowdown catches nothing.

build/Show the free disk.note: df only; nothing is deleted, the runner has ~90GB free

build/Restore the git store.note: was 30. A download of the 0.3-1.5GB store from GitHub's cache service, not work of ours: over the last 56 builds of pages.yml (runs 45555459731..45603088923) median 10s, p90 19s, p95 21s, and one 32s (run 45602452354) that failed the old 30s, with no store growth behind it (the next build restored in 23s, the one before in 11s). The slow tail is the cache service, so 60 = 1.9x the slowest seen and 2x the p95 of 21s; a restore that is slow every time, not once in 56, will still cross it

build/Check out.note: was 30. Two paths, measured over the last 100 runs of pages.yml (12 real build jobs): warm incremental fetch 9-12s (10 runs); and the store reset, where Check out finds the restored git store over 1500MB, drops .git and fetches from scratch, 91s and 94s (runs 40267913545, 40276271478). The store restarts at 335MB and grew to 1397MB and then 1660MB across the builds between resets, so the reset recurs about every 6th build (2 in 12): expected work, not runner variance, and it failed 2 of 12 builds against the old 30s. 150 = 1.6x the slowest reset seen (94s). The warm path is far under it (p99 12s); a warm-path regression now shows only as the step nearing 94s, which is the price of one row for both paths

build/Start the build path probe.incremental: reads only the git diff between two commits' trees (ci_scope.py), never a puzzle file
build/Start the build path probe.note: only starts tools/probe_path.sh in the background and returns; its time (the live commit, a blobless fetch, the diff: 23s on the critical path in run 44984839816) is hidden behind the cache restores, and Choose the build path waits for what is left

build/Restore the row cache.note: now only starts a background restore (tools/cache_bg.sh); the wait for it is in the Wait step after the starts

build/Restore the clue index.note: now only starts a background restore (tools/cache_bg.sh); the wait for it is in the Wait step after the starts

build/Build the authored puzzle.note: 2s on a warm clue index (run 38378765553); 31s cold, which the explicit Save the clue index now prevents

build/Restore the puzzle shims.note: now only starts a background restore (tools/cache_bg.sh); the wait for it is in the Wait step after the starts; the shims are unpacked by the same background job (tools/cache_tar.sh)

build/Wait for the puzzle shims.note: what is left of the shim restore and unpack. Was 19s + 14s in series as steps of their own

build/Warm the row cache, slice 1 of 8.note: was 100: run 44980902460 (full build, 11-22) took 103-104s on slice 1 and 93-95s on slices 2-8 as the corpus grew; 125 = 1.2x 104. was 80: slices 1-3 took 81-83s cold in run 43436516329 (full build, 11-13) as the corpus grew; 100 = 1.2x 83. was 60. build/Start the reindex.note: only starts the reindex in the background and returns; its time shows in Build the puzzle shims and reindex, which waits for it after the social card and page restores it runs beside

build/Wait for the social cards and the.note: what is left of those two restores, which ran since the job's checkout beside everything before the reindex. Was 20s + 2s in series as steps of their own

build/Build the puzzle shims and reindex.note: 17-21s on warm shims and rows (runs 38378765553, 38385076152); 56-127s cold (127s in run 38390532020). Was 75, under that cold range: an edit to code the index rows reach (the format converter, run 38383021945) re-makes all ~51k rows by design and took 94s, so every such push went red for expected work. Was 150: 19-39s on 22 of 24 builds 2026-10-25..29 (median 31s), but a scheduled build reindexes every puzzle changed since the last deploy, and GitHub throttles the 15-minute cron to one build every few hours, so the batch is whatever the burn pushed meanwhile: 659 changed puzzles (twice any other batch seen) took 153s in run 40950475350. 190 = 1.2x that

build/Restore the social cards.note: now only starts a background restore (tools/cache_bg.sh); the wait for it is in the Wait step after the starts

build/Draw the social cards.note: was 450: 471s in run 43436516329 (full build, 11-13) as the corpus grew; 570 = 1.21x 471. Was 360: a push touching tools re-listed every row and drew 120 cards in 368s (run 43223109759; 341s in run 43219464745 hours earlier), the worst case growing with the corpus; 450 = 1.22x 368. Was 900: the card key hashed make_og_card.py's bytes, so any edit redrew all ~17k cards 600 a run (816s, run 38370347047). Now keyed on the card's rendered HTML: steady state is the cached list (~15-40s) plus the cards a push moved; worst case a code edit re-lists every row (~60s) and draws OG_LIMIT=120 cards at ~0.9s each. Was 240: with a cold row cache the re-list took 146s and the 120 cards 100s (246s, run 39653095057), as the corpus grew. Was 300: a scheduled run after a day of annotate-code edits re-listed every row in 223s on a warm row cache, then drew 120 cards in 102s (329s, run 40199706228)

build/Name the puzzle pages' key.uncached: it runs before Restore the puzzle pages, to name that cache's key; --fingerprint hashes only the page code (tools/page_cache.py), never the puzzle files, though the lint sees cache_warmth.py as a corpus tool
build/Name the puzzle pages' key.note: hashes the page code once (tools/cache_warmth.py --fingerprint) so Restore and Save the puzzle pages use one key; a few seconds of python

build/Expose the cache credentials.note: a local node action (.github/actions/cache-env) that copies the cache service's token into the job's environment for tools/cache_bg.sh

build/Restore the puzzle pages.note: now only starts a background restore (tools/cache_bg.sh); the wait for it is in the Wait step after the starts; the pages and the page store are unpacked by the same background job (tools/cache_tar.sh)

build/Generate the crawlable pages, shar.note: was 6 shards, 93-96s on every one in the first cold build over 60k pages (run 42540698988: 9954 pages a shard, 84s of render plus 7s startup, ~8.4ms a page). 6 shards had been sized for ~62s cold on ~54k pages; corpus growth (+12%) and a higher per-page cost pushed a cold build over 90. Warm builds are 21-32s over 51 runs (max 32), so this bites only when a page-code change re-renders everything. All six shards were equal, so not runner variance: the answer is more shards, not a bigger budget. 9 shards of ~6.7k pages is ~63s cold, 1.4x under the unchanged 90s, room for ~40% more corpus before the next split. A ninth of the puzzle pages (--shard 0/9, by a hash of the id)

build/Wait for the row, clue and page ca.note: what is left of the row cache, clue index and page store restores (and the page unpack) after Install Pillow and the probe, which they ran beside. Bimodal with the same cache entries: 29-32s on some runners, 59-67s on others, where every phase runs about twice as slow (row cache download, page and shim tar). 90 = 1.34x the 67s slow mode

build/Choose the build path.incremental: reads only the git diff between two commits' trees (ci_scope.py), never a puzzle file
build/Choose the build path.note: the puzzle fast path's test (tools/ci_scope.py against the last deployed commit): a few gh api calls and one blobless fetch of that commit's trees. Run 39360349916 spent 37s of its 37s in that fetch (no checkout; the log is silent until it prints), a base 82 paths behind: the fetch of a ~54k-file tree set grows with how far the deployed commit is, so 30s was too tight; 60s still catches a regression

build/Generate the crawlable pages (puzz.note: replaces the 8 warming slices, 6 page shards and Assemble on a push that only changed puzzle files (Choose the build path). The 4 shards plus the assemble took ~87s warm (run 39236355785) of which ~40s was workers piping each reused page's blocks back; build_seo_pages --reuse-first checks the stored pages in the parent and renders only the rest. Was 60, the assemble's: on the scheduled builds that deploy the burn's puzzle pushes it took 38-73s over 12 runs (2026-10-25..29), red in 3 (64, 64, 73s), and the time does not track the work: 1725 pages rendered in 51s (run 40609173036), 538 in 64s (run 40902755722). Runner variance on a fixed ~50s, so 90 = 1.2x the slowest 73s, the full path's shard budget. Raised to 150 on 2026-11-11: 10 puzzle-push runs 2026-11-12 (UTC) 01:04..04:45 took 73-137s warm (median 90.5s; 81, 77, 80, 85, 73, 137, 120, 96s) with two cold-cache outliers (511s, 545s); run 43154624689 went red at 96s with no change to build_seo_pages.py since 11-10 (its commit 0ea9595 only annotated one puzzle), so it is runner/load variance and growth of the corpus, not a regression. 150 = 1.1x the slowest warm 137s

build/Assemble the crawlable pages.note: was 80: 54-82s over the 15 full builds 2026-11-23..25 whose step data is still served (median 69; 54, 59, 63, 65, 65, 67, 68, 69, 70, 70, 72, 73, 75, 78, 82; the 82s is run 45644316571, 78s run 45495143958), no jump at any commit, up from the 46-63s (median 56) below as the corpus grew; 100 = 1.2x 82. Puzzle pushes take the fast path and skip this step. was 60: 46-63s over 24 full builds 2026-11-04 (median 56, 63s in run 41801983040), no jump at any commit, so 80 = 1.25x the 63s max. The serial tail (hub, listings, sitemaps, ~10s of CPU) after the shards, and the check that every page was rendered by exactly one of them. Replaces the one 160s step, Generate the crawlable pages

build/Restore the IndexNow manifest.note: now only starts a background restore (tools/cache_bg.sh); the wait for it is in the Wait step after the starts

build/List the site.uncached: lists the published files by glob; it opens none of them
build/List the site.note: was 20: 7-17s in 22 of 23 recent builds (median 11), 30s in one (the run after a cold render wrote ~138k files), so 20 sat 3s over the normal worst and failed on disk-cache luck, not a regression. 45 = 1.5x the 30s max. Globs PUBLISH and writes the tar list. Was Stage the site, 45s: 23s hard-linking ~138k files into _site/ and 22s checking links (run 38385716791)

build/Start the site checks.uncached: starts the checks Wait for the site checks collects, and returns
build/Start the site checks.note: only starts the link check and the IndexNow hashing in the background; their time shows in Wait for the site checks

build/Archive the site.note: was 45: 11 of 12 recent builds took 22-37s, one (run 45074270698) took 53s while Upload the site in the same run also ran 46s against its usual 35s, so a slow runner and not a slower step; 60 = 1.1x that outlier, 1.6x the slowest ordinary build. Earlier: tar of the ~4.7GB, ~295k-entry site into /dev/shm: 18-19s. Into the runner disk it was 17-56s, bound by the disk; if the site outgrows /dev/shm it falls back to the disk, and this budget will say so. 45 = 2.4x 19, room for the slow runner mode that doubles the cache restores

build/Upload the site.warn: actions/upload-artifact sending the stored (level 0) tar to GitHub, so the time is GitHub's upload and not our work: 26-40s over 21 push builds and 35-38s over 2 scheduled builds 2026-10-29..30 (median 35s, only 5s under the budget), with one 72s outlier (run 41005868629) for the same artifact; a 40s fail would go red on ordinary variance
build/Upload the site.note: 39s at deflate level 1 (run 38378765553), 65s at level 6; stored (level 0) 18s (run 38380967725)

build/Wait for the site checks.uncached: the link check reads every published page (stage_site.py --check, across the cores) and IndexNow hashes them; they run beside Archive and Upload, so this is only what is left over
build/Wait for the site checks.note: was the check half of Stage the site (22s) plus List the changed pages (8s), in series in front of the upload

deploy/Deploy to Pages.warn: GitHub's Pages deploy: 71-437s over 24 builds 2026-10-25..29, over 180 in 5 (208, 334, 362, 437s on scheduled builds, 191s on a push) for the same ~2GB artifact; we only wait on GitHub here, and the artifact size is what we control (Upload the site, Archive the site)
deploy/Deploy to Pages.note: GitHub side: 69-134s (134s in run 38391832453, same artifact) for the 2.5GB, ~138k-file artifact (runs 38385076152, 38385716791, 38383021945); scales with what is shipped, not with what changed

deploy/Deploy to Pages (retry).warn: only runs after the first Deploy to Pages attempt stalled and was cut at 300s; the action's own 600s timeout bounds it
deploy/Deploy to Pages (retry).note: a stalled GitHub deploy (6 runs on 2026-11-07); a normal deploy never reaches this step

deploy/Wait for the build's site.note: tools/wait_for_build.py: the deploy job starts with the checks and waits for the build job's site, so this is the build's own time (up to its 90-minute cap), bounded by the step's 60-minute timeout

build/Save the git store.note: was 45. An upload of the same store to the cache service: over the last 55 builds median 9s, p90 19s, p95 24s, and one 61s (run 45601424272, 6.8x the median) that failed the old 45s; the store was not larger than in the runs around it (Restore 11s, Check out 11s in that run, next save 8s). The slow tail is the cache service, so 90 = 1.5x the slowest seen and 3.8x the p95; a save that is slow every time, not once in 55, will still cross it

build/Save the row cache.note: now only starts a background save (tools/cache_bg.sh), which waits for the site checks and starts after Upload the site; the time is in Wait for the cache saves

build/Save the clue index.note: now only starts a background save (tools/cache_bg.sh), which waits for the site checks and starts after Upload the site; the time is in Wait for the cache saves

build/Save the puzzle shims.note: now only starts a background save (tools/cache_bg.sh), which waits for the site checks and starts after Upload the site; the time is in Wait for the cache saves; the background job packs the shims first (tools/cache_tar.sh)

build/Save the social cards.note: now only starts a background save (tools/cache_bg.sh), which waits for the site checks and starts after Upload the site; the time is in Wait for the cache saves. Before that, 15s, 27s, 68s (run 44624440086, 11-19), 95s (run 44692316707, 11-20) as a step of its own

build/Save the IndexNow manifest.note: now only starts a background save (tools/cache_bg.sh), which waits for the site checks and starts after Upload the site; the time is in Wait for the cache saves

build/Wait for the cache saves.note: what is left of the six background saves (and the packing of the shims and pages), which start after Upload the site and run beside the steps that follow it; they wait for the site checks first

build/Save the puzzle pages.note: now only starts a background save (tools/cache_bg.sh), which waits for the site checks and starts after Upload the site; the time is in Wait for the cache saves; the background job packs the pages first. Runs only after a render of over 800 pages (a code change, a cold cache)

budgets/Check out.note: depth 1, sparse to tools + .github/workflows, as validate does

validate/Check out.note: already depth 1, blob:none, sparse to tools + .github/workflows; still 65s and 74s (runs 38636406433, 38635950789) as the tools tree grew. 1.5x the observed 74s

validate/Choose what to check.note: a full check fetches the whole tree here, in eight streams (four until 2026-11-10); 155 is 1.2x the 129s worst of 34 full checks on 2026-11-10 (88-129s with four streams, the tree grown by the burn; over 110 in run 42870063495); the diff and the scope are a few seconds. Was 75: full checks took 67-89s on 2026-10-22 (89s in run 39799670301, 76s in the red run 39796038374); 110 is 1.2x the 89s
